advisory: August 2026. The fleet runs tollbooth-dpyc 0.80.0, pinned by all 12 consumers. 0.80.0 fixed a blind spot in the surface operators use to audit their own tools: a handler reachable on the wire but missing from the ToolIdentity table was listed by tools/list, refused at debit time as tool_not_registered, and yet absent from list_canonical_identities — so Pricing Studio's Reconcile, which joins against that listing, reported clean and the first real signal was a patron-facing denial. The listing now checks the live surface from two sides (the @paid_tool UUID map and the live FastMCP tool names, since neither alone is complete) and reports every drifting tool once, at the richest detail available, in an unregistered array. Its own tool id also moved to capability v5, the last hand-written v4 in the standard catalog; LEGACY_TOOL_ID_ALIASES rewrites stored pricing rows on load, so no operator re-prices. 0.79.0 made a delivered credential actually take effect: the async-executor resolution cached a definitive answer once and the executor it built carried the API key baked in at construction, so delivering or rotating the long-runner secrets did nothing until the container was replaced — a server holding an expired key kept presenting it, failed every dispatch, and fell back to in-process execution on a recycling front while service_status still reported the executor active. Credential receipt now invalidates both caches, a degraded dispatch reports itself in its result, and service_status distinguishes an executor being installed from it actually dispatching. 0.78.0 gave the OAuth code-to-token exchange the same fault taxonomy the refresh path got in 0.77.0: a 400 from a provider token endpoint now names its own cause (oauth_exchange_grant_rejected / _request_malformed / _unavailable) instead of collapsing into a blind 'token exchange failed, check operator logs' with the provider's reason discarded unread. It also finished the ledger write-through migration begun in 0.62.0 — a CAS conflict on flush used to retry the same stale snapshot, which can never satisfy the guard, stranding settlements, restores and invoice retirement unflushable for the life of the process. 0.77.0 named five more OAuth failures that all reported that your access had expired. 0.75.0 taught a vault read to say WHY it could not answer instead of reporting 'you never authorized'; 0.76.0 split three OAuth situations that all used to reach patrons as 'your access expired' — a refresh now happens one patron at a time (concurrent publishers were spending one single-use rotating refresh token N times), an incomplete refresh is the retryable oauth_refresh_unavailable, and a rejected ACCESS token is oauth_token_rejected, which retires its own cached expiry so the next call renews. Only a provider naming the grant dead still yields oauth_token_expired. Earlier history, since 0.52: 0.53.x added a generic upstream-402 handler (a bare 402 means renew-subscription, distinct from x402 payment); 0.57.0 unified the identity-proof token as a single dpop_token (was proof_token / poison / proof); 0.58.0 and 0.59.0 gave claim-check async jobs an adaptive poll cadence and an optional author-declared time budget; 0.59.1 fixed the machine-to-machine certify path to send dpop_token (not the retired proof kwarg), which had blocked patron credit purchases. NETWORK MINIMUM is 0.49.0: operators below it read the legacy kind-4 bootstrap DM and cannot bootstrap against the current Authorities, which publish bootstrap config only as the NIP-33 kind-30078 replaceable event. HISTORICAL SECURITY FLOOR: v0.44.2 fixed a credential-card redemption leak (receive_credentials could echo raw values) — never run below it. NEW HOST: the network now has a second operator host, tollbooth-wasmcp (SpinOperatorHost) 0.1.5 — the Spin/WASI peer of FastMCP. tollbooth-fermyon is the first Spin operator: the same operator source as tollbooth-sample, running in WebAssembly at the edge, validated end-to-end (proof, Secure Courier, Lightning, billed call).
architecture_notes: Schema symmetry: every operator and Authority gets its own Neon schema; credentials live in an encrypted_blob column. vault_source and purchase_mode are independent axes (a sub-Authority self-provisions its Neon from env yet still certifies up). Each service reports its version in service_status from its own pyproject [project].version (installed metadata, with a from-source pyproject.toml fallback) — there is no hand-maintained version constant to drift. Standard tool bodies live in tested tollbooth.tools.* modules behind thin proof-gate shims; tool names and behavior are unchanged. Operators run on one of two hosts from the same source: FastMCP (on Prefect Horizon) or the Spin/WASI SpinOperatorHost (tollbooth-wasmcp); the Spin host carries the WASI seams (crypto component, relay bridge, nsec-only bootstrap) so the operator stays business-logic only.
